title: fix(plugin-security)!: row-scope the private credential tables (sys_verification, sys_jwks) in every shipped set
body:
Fixes #20027

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## What was wrong

`sys_verification` (one-time verification and password-reset tokens) and `sys_jwks` (the environment's JWT signing keys) both declare `access: { default: 'private' }`, and `default-permission-sets.ts` has always documented them as "DENY for non-admins by design". The shipped permission sets did not hold that.

Both objects are on `BETTER_AUTH_MANAGED_OBJECTS`, so `denyWritesOnManagedObjects()` gives every shipped set that spreads the blanket an **explicit** per-object read entry (`allowRead: true`). The `private` posture only keeps a plain `'*'` wildcard off an object (`resolveObjectPermission`); it does not touch an explicit entry. Neither object carried a row policy, and the wildcard `tenant_isolation` policy that once denied their rows retired with ADR-0095 D1 (Layer 0 is inert on an object with no tenant column). So the object-level read resolved `true` for every non-admin set and nothing narrowed it.

## Reachability, measured before the fix

Measured on the real `SecurityPlugin` + `ObjectQL` over a real driver, with the shipped permission sets, across the five non-admin shipped personas (`member_default`, `viewer_readonly`, `organization_admin`, `organization_admin_no_bypass`, and `mcp_agent_data_write` acting for a member). The full surface-by-surface table is on the card. In summary, verdicts only:

- Engine read: **reachable** for every non-admin persona, for both objects.
- `sys_verification`: reachable through the generic data route and through object-generic readers (analytics; reports where composed).
- `sys_jwks`: reachable through the object-generic readers only (its generic-data-route and MCP surfaces are closed by the object's own declarations).
- MCP data tools, global search, related-record expansion, share links and batch/realtime: not reachable.

Every reachable surface funnels through the one engine read-filter path, so all of them close with a single instrument.

## Fix

The instrument the file header names: a per-object row scope, and no edit of the blanket. A new `privateCredentialRowScope()` returns a `select` policy that admits no row (`id == null`, the `_none` shape PR #20023 uses) for each of `sys_verification` and `sys_jwks`, spread into every shipped set that spreads the blanket and carries row-level security — `organization_admin` (and so its derived `organization_admin_no_bypass`), `member_default` and `viewer_readonly`.

- There is no `_self` form: neither table names a user, and no principal below platform admin needs to read even their own live token.
- `admin_full_access` is unchanged: its wildcard carries the superuser read bypass, which skips the row layer, and it names neither object explicitly. The platform admin still reads every row.
- better-auth's own flows are unchanged: it reads and writes these tables through its adapter under system context, which no row policy reaches.
- The MCP write ceiling holds the blanket too and carries no row policy of its own by design (ADR-0090 D10); its bound is the delegating user's sets, which now carry the scope. Measured, not assumed.
- Why every set carries the scope and not the baseline alone: with `fallbackPermissionSet: null` no platform baseline is composed, and a set with no policy for an object leaves that object unfiltered.

Why a row policy rather than a precedence change in the evaluator: three other `private` objects on the blanket — `sys_device_code`, `sys_oauth_access_token`, `sys_oauth_refresh_token` — are deliberately readable by their owner through the same explicit entry plus a `_self` policy. Making the evaluator refuse a managed-list explicit entry on a `private` object would retire those reads too. The row scope touches only the two objects the contract names.

## Tests

Driven on the real `SecurityPlugin` + `ObjectQL` over a real `SqlDriver`, with the shipped sets, in three deployment shapes (stock `isolated`, `isolated` with no baseline, `single`) — the shapes PR #20023's test covers.

- New: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/private-credential-row-scope.test.ts` (37 tests). Every non-admin persona reads 0 rows of both objects (list, count and by-id, including its own verification row). Controls: the platform admin reads every row list and by-id, and better-auth's adapter (system context) reads every row by identifier and by id.
- The probe was committed first, on the pre-fix tree, where its persona cases were red (`Tests 28 failed | 9 passed`).
- Re-judged, not deleted: `objects/rbac-objects.test.ts`'s `member_default` policy-name list gains `sys_jwks_none` and `sys_verification_none`, with a note.
- `@objectstack/plugin-security`, full suite: `Test Files 131 passed (131) · Tests 2598 passed (2598)`.
- `@objectstack/plugin-security` typecheck, all three tsc programs plus `check:test-typecheck`: exit 0, "0 file(s) / 0 error(s)". The new test file is in the test tsc program (`--listFiles`).
- `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, full suite (its adapter reads these tables; its vitest config aliases plugin-security to source): `Test Files 114 passed (114) · Tests 2439 passed (2439)`.
- Other consumers naming either object in a test (`objectql`, `platform-objects`, `plugin-pinyin-search`, `rest`, `spec`): none pins the shipped sets' policy names or reads a row of these tables under a user context; declared to CI.

### Ablation of every negative pin

The fix was committed before any ablation. Each ablation mutated the committed `default-permission-sets.ts` through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (on-disk anchor-hit and blob-change proof), ran the probe, then restored; every restore proven as blob `37920bbfa764` == HEAD with `git diff HEAD` empty.

| ablation | result |
|---|---|
| A1 remove the spread from `member_default` | 10 failed: `member_default` and the MCP agent (both composed shapes) |
| A2 remove the spread from `organization_admin` | 4 failed: `organization_admin` and `organization_admin_no_bypass`, no-baseline shape only |
| A3 remove the spread from `viewer_readonly` | 2 failed: `viewer_readonly`, no-baseline shape only |
| A4 delete the `sys_verification_none` policy | 28 failed: every persona in every shape |
| A5 delete the `sys_jwks_none` policy | 28 failed: every persona in every shape |

## Changeset

`.changeset/20027-private-credential-objects.md`, `@objectstack/plugin-security: minor`, a `!` headline, the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line, a **BREAKING** paragraph naming what a non-admin can no longer read and the remedy, and the honest ADR-0087 marker (`not-required`, no migration prescription — the sets are code evaluated from the in-memory declaration).

## Gates

- 61 exited 0. `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET` — needs a whole-repo `dist/`), declared to CI.
- `GITHUB_TOKEN=… node scripts/check-issue-citations.mjs`: exit 0, 5 citations resolve.
- ESLint, narrowed to the three changed TypeScript files (`--no-inline-config --format json`): 3 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. The config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`), so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **The class recurs by construction** (unchanged from PR #20023's note): at `kernel:ready`, `applyManagedWriteDenies` gives every registered `managedBy: 'better-auth'` object an `allowRead: true` entry on the target sets, so the next `private` managed table arrives readable by every member unless its author also adds a row scope here. No guard is added; new gates default to no. Carrier: whoever adds the next private managed object.
- `sys_secret` (`managedBy: 'engine-owned'`) is `private` too but is NOT on this blanket, so it is not part of this class and was not measured here.
